אליה כבר אישר את הכיוון. תתחילי ממכירות.

- onecli-gateway: OneCLI Gateway: transparent HTTPS proxy that injects stored credentials into outbound calls. You MUST use this skill when the user asks you to read emails, check calendar, access GitHub repos, create issues, check Stripe payments, or interact with ANY external service or API. Do NOT use browser extensions or OAuth CLI tools. Make HTTP requests directly; the gateway injects credentials automatically.
- self-customize: Customize your own agent — add capabilities, install packages, add MCP servers, edit code or CLAUDE.md. Use when the user asks you to add a feature, install a tool, or modify how you work. For non-trivial code changes, delegate to a builder agent via create_agent.
- slack-formatting: Format messages for Slack using mrkdwn syntax. Use when responding to Slack channels (folder starts with "slack_" or JID contains slack identifiers).
- vercel-cli: Deploy apps to Vercel. Use when asked to deploy, ship, or publish a web application, or manage Vercel projects, domains, and environment variables.
- welcome: Introduce yourself to a newly connected channel. Triggered automatically when a channel is first wired. Send a friendly greeting and brief overview of what you can do.
- whatsapp-formatting: Format messages for WhatsApp, including mentions that render as real WhatsApp tags. Use when responding in a WhatsApp conversation (platform_id / chatJid ends with @s.whatsapp.net or @g.us).
- deep-research: Deep research harness — fan-out web searches, fetch sources, adversarially verify claims, synthesize a cited report. - When the user wants a deep, multi-source, fact-checked research report on any topic. BEFORE invoking, check if the question is specific enough to research directly — if underspecified (e.g., "what car to buy" without budget/use-case/region), ask 2-3 clarifying questions to narrow scope. Then pass the refined question as args, weaving the answers in.
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- verify: Verify that a code change actually does what it's supposed to by running the app and observing behavior. Use when asked to verify a PR, confirm a fix works, test a change manually, check that a feature works, or validate local changes before pushing.
- code-review: Review the current diff for correctness bugs and reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups at the given effort level (low/medium: fewer, high-confidence findings; high→max: broader coverage, may include uncertain findings). Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review.
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo, defaults to 10m) - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- schedule: Create, update, list, or run scheduled remote agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule. - When the user wants to schedule a recurring remote agent, set up automated tasks, create a cron job for Claude Code, or manage their scheduled agents/routines. Also use when the user wants a one-time scheduled run ("run this once at 3pm", "remind me to check X tomorrow").

TRIGGER when: code imports `anthropic`/`@anthropic-ai/sdk`; user asks for the Claude API, Anthropic SDK, or Managed Agents; user adds/modifies/tunes a Claude feature (caching, thinking, compaction, tool use, batch, files, citations, memory) or model (Opus/Sonnet/Haiku) in a file; questions about prompt caching / cache hit rate in an Anthropic SDK project.

- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).

# Role → Agent-Spec Engine (canonical)

**Purpose:** the post-install value layer. Once a user installed NanoClaw via the guide, this is *what they do with it* — a per-role agent that runs the **methodologies** (multi-step professional workflows) of their job. (Strategy origin: Elia #3264-#3274.)

**The unlock (Elia #3272):** don't hand-build 2-4 methodologies × 15 roles. Build ONE repeatable engine. **The engine already exists internally = NanoCo's profiling framework** (`methodology.md`, Alex's domain): the **4 Profiling Pillars**. Run the pillars on a role → out comes the agent spec.

---

## THE ENGINE — 4 Pillars → Agent Spec

| Pillar | Profiling question | Produces |
|--------|--------------------|----------|
| **Role** | purpose, success metric, who they report to | framing / north-star |
| **Routines** | recurring triggers, daily moments, deadlines | **the core moments = the methodologies** |
| **Systems** | platforms used, manual workarounds | **tools/connections** (Gmail/CRM/Calendar → our connection guides) |
| **Skills** | domain terms, decision rules, automation priorities | **the sequence/playbook per moment** + the calibration |

**Focus principle:** 2-4 CORE methodologies per role only — the spine, ranked by frequency × value. Not everything.

---

## OUTPUT FORMAT — what every role produces

### A. Role profile (4 pillars applied)
- **Role:** one line purpose + success metric
- **Routines:** ranked list of recurring moments (the methodology candidates)
- **Systems:** tools the role lives in
- **Skills:** domain vocabulary + the professional sequence each core moment triggers

### B. Agent spec (derived from the profile)
- **2-4 methodologies**, each: `trigger → sequence → output → tools needed → day-one or needs-connection`
- **Calibration** = a mini self-profiling (same 4 pillars, lightweight) the END USER does at install → personalizes the generic role-spec to *them* (what you sell, who your customer is, which CRM, paste a past email so I learn your voice)
- **Paste-once "teach your agent this" block** = the MVP delivery; NanoClaw internalizes it as a standing skill. Phase 2 = a real installable skill.

**Two profiling layers:** WE profile the generic role archetype (once, per role). The USER profiles themselves (calibration, at install). The first makes it professional; the second makes it theirs.

---

## PRODUCTION PIPELINE (how we crank all 15 roles)
1. **Draft** the profile via domain research + the existing role-page use-cases (AI first pass through the 4 pillars).
2. **Enrich** with Alex's real interview/field data where available (she's the profiling agent; this is her domain).
3. **Validate** the core moments + sequences with Elia / domain expert (the sales validation = the pattern).
4. **Generate** the calibration questions + the paste-once block.
5. **Build** into the guide engine (post-install / per-role).

---

## TEMPLATE ROLE: SALES (proven first run)

### Profile
- **Role:** win deals — move prospects from contact to signed. Success = pipeline converted, deals closed.
- **Routines (core moments):** (1) פנייה ראשונה/פרוספקטינג · (2) סיום שיחה · (3) הצעת מחיר · (4) ניהול פולו-אפ לאורך זמן
- **Systems:** CRM, email, calendar, content/case-study library, messaging (WhatsApp/LinkedIn)
- **Skills:** discovery questioning, objection handling, funnel-stage awareness, follow-up cadence, quote/pricing structure, voice/tone

### Methodologies (full detail in `sales_methodologies_v1.md`)
1. **פנייה ראשונה** — research lead → identify pain → draft opener in your voice → right first ask → follow-up reminder
2. **סיום שיחה** — structured summary → CRM log → follow-up email → team brief → pull matching case → next-step reminder
3. **הצעת מחיר** — pull needs from call summary → build tailored quote (your pricing/template/voice) → suggest tiers
4. **ניהול פולו-אפ** — review open leads → flag cold/due → draft per-funnel-stage follow-up → prioritized daily list

### Calibration (user answers once at install)
- מה אתה מוכר ולמי? · איזה CRM אתה משתמש? · מה טווח המחירים / יש תבנית הצעה? · תדביק מייל/הצעה ישנים שאלמד את הקול שלך · מה מחזור הפולו-אפ הטבעי שלך (ימים)?

---

## STATUS
- Engine direction LOCKED by Elia #3274 ("בול, צא לדרך").
- Alex being brought in as profiling source/validator (her domain).
- NEXT: lock sales spec with Elia → build sales end-to-end (paste block + calibration) as the proven template → run pipeline for remaining roles.

### Pillar 1 — Role
- **Purpose:** Move prospects from first contact to signed deal. [A]
- **Success metric:** Pipeline conversion rate, deals closed (volume + value), quota attainment. [A]
- **Reports to:** Sales Manager / VP Sales (in most orgs). [A]
- **Who depends on them:** SDR who hands off leads, CS/onboarding who inherits the closed deal, management who reads pipeline health. [A]

---

### Pillar 2 — Routines (core moments, ranked by frequency × value)

| Rank | Moment | Frequency | Agent value |
|------|--------|-----------|-------------|
| 1 | ניהול פולו-אפ | Daily | High — most reps drop ball here [A] |
| 2 | הכנה לשיחה | Per-meeting | High — skipped under time pressure, hurts call quality [A] |
| 3 | סיום שיחה | Per-meeting | Highest per-event — CRM lag + weak summaries are universal [A] |
| 4 | פנייה ראשונה | Weekly/per-lead | High — personalization takes long, generic openers underperform [A] |
| 5 | הצעת מחיר | Per-opportunity | Medium — high-stakes, but less frequent [A] |

---

### Pillar 3 — Systems

| System | What reps do in it | Notes |
|--------|-------------------|-------|
| CRM (Salesforce / HubSpot / Pipedrive) | Log activities, update stages, view pipeline, set tasks | Most-used, most-complained-about. Often laggy or incomplete. [A] |
| Email (Gmail / Outlook) | Outreach, follow-ups, proposals | Primary async channel. [A] |
| Calendar (Google / Outlook) | Schedule calls, set reminders, see daily load | Trigger source for prep + follow-up. [A] |
| Case/content library (Drive / Notion / SharePoint) | Pull case studies, decks, pricing templates | Often ad-hoc; location varies by company. [A] |
| Messaging (WhatsApp / LinkedIn) | Outreach, informal follow-up | Increasingly primary in Israeli market. [A] |

**Calibration note:** CRM tool, content library location, and messaging preference must be confirmed per user at install.

---

### Pillar 4 — Skills

| Skill | Where it lives in workflow | Agent role |
|-------|--------------------------|------------|
| Discovery questioning | Pillar 2 → Methodology 2 (Prep) | Prepare questions before call, not improvise during [A] |
| Objection handling | Pillar 2 → Methodology 3 (End-of-call debrief) | Help formulate written response to objection raised in call [A] |
| Funnel-stage awareness | All follow-up methodologies | Determines which follow-up type and tone apply [A] |
| Follow-up cadence | Methodology 5 | Rep's personal rhythm (days between touches); calibrated at install [A] |
| Quote/pricing structure | Methodology 4 | Needs rep's actual pricing template / tiers [A] |
| Voice/tone | All outbound messages | Learned from pasted past emails at install [A] |

---

## SECTION B — Agent Spec (5 Methodologies)

---

### Methodology 1 — פנייה ראשונה (First Outreach)

**Trigger:** New lead added to CRM / new contact identified for outreach [A]

**Sequence:**
1. Pull lead info (role, company, size, recent news if findable) [A]
2. Identify likely pain point based on ICP and what rep is selling [A]
3. Match to one relevant case study or proof point [A]
4. Draft personalized opener in rep's voice — one clear value statement, one soft first ask (call, question, resource) [A]
5. Set follow-up reminder in CRM if no reply within rep's cadence [A]

**Output:** Draft first-touch message (email or WhatsApp) + CRM reminder

**Tools needed:** CRM, email/WhatsApp, case library

**Day-one or needs-connection:** Needs CRM connection + rep voice sample (paste at calibration)

---

### Methodology 2 — הכנה לשיחה (Pre-Call Prep) ⬅ NEW

**Trigger:** Meeting/call scheduled — calendar event created or CRM task set [A]

**Sequence:**
1. Pull account history from CRM — last interaction, open notes, current stage [A]
2. Check for recent news about the company or contact (new funding, product launch, leadership change) [A]
3. Review last call summary / email thread for open threads and promises made [A]
4. Generate discovery questions tailored to what's still unknown at this stage [A] ← *discovery questioning skill anchored here*
5. Pull 1-2 relevant case studies or proof points matched to known pain / industry [A]
6. Set agenda: what's the goal of this call, what's the one ask at the end [A]

**Output:** Pre-call brief — 1 page: account snapshot, key open questions, relevant cases, call goal

**Tools needed:** CRM, calendar, case library, (optional: web search for news)

**Day-one or needs-connection:** CRM connection required; case library location confirmed at calibration

---

### Methodology 3 — סיום שיחה (Post-Call Close)

**Trigger:** Call ends [A]

**Sequence:**
1. Write structured call summary: what was said, what was revealed about pain/budget/authority/timeline, what was agreed [A]
2. Log to CRM: activity logged, stage updated, next task set [A]
3. Draft follow-up email: recap agreed next steps, attach any promised materials, clear CTA [A]
4. **If an objection came up:** debrief — identify the objection, draft a written response for inclusion in follow-up or future calls [A] ← *objection handling skill anchored here*
5. Pull matching case study if a specific concern surfaced [A]
6. Brief team if deal involves others (e.g., "looping in our technical contact") [A]
7. Set next-step reminder [A]

**Output:** CRM log + follow-up email + internal brief (when relevant) + objection response (when relevant)

**Tools needed:** CRM, email, case library, messaging

**Day-one or needs-connection:** CRM connection required; email connection required

---

### Methodology 4 — הצעת מחיר (Proposal)

**Trigger:** Call summary contains positive signal ("send me a quote") or rep marks stage as proposal-ready [A]

**Sequence:**
1. Pull needs, constraints, and priorities from call summary [A]
2. Apply to rep's pricing template / tiers [A]
3. Tailor framing — lead with the pain they named, connect to the right tier [A]
4. Suggest optional add-ons or tiers if applicable [A]
5. Draft proposal cover note in rep's voice — warm, clear, low-friction next step [A]

**Output:** Proposal document (filled template) + cover email

**Tools needed:** Quote/pricing template, email, CRM

**Day-one or needs-connection:** Needs rep's pricing template pasted or connected at calibration

---

### Methodology 5 — ניהול פולו-אפ (Follow-Up Management)

Three distinct sub-types. The agent identifies which applies by reading CRM stage + days since last contact + last interaction type.

---

#### 5a — Re-engagement (lead went cold)

**Trigger:** Open lead with no activity in [X] days (X = calibrated follow-up cadence) and no reply to prior outreach [A]

**Sequence:**
1. Check last interaction — what was the last message, what was the ask [A]
2. Assess: still worth pursuing? (stage, deal size, ICP fit) [A]
3. Draft re-engagement message that adds new value — new angle, relevant news hook, new case study — NOT a repeat of the last message [A]
4. If second re-engagement also receives no reply → flag lead as dormant, suggest pipeline cleanup [A]

**Output:** Re-engagement message (or dormant flag + recommended action)

**Tools needed:** CRM, email/WhatsApp

---

#### 5b — Nurture (proposal sent, no response)

**Trigger:** Proposal sent [X] days ago, deal still open, no response [A]

**Sequence:**
1. Check if proposal was opened (if email tracking is available) [A]
2. Draft soft check-in that adds value — answer a likely concern, reference a relevant outcome, acknowledge their timeline without pressure [A]
3. Single clear low-friction ask (e.g., "Is this still on your radar?" / "Happy to adjust anything") [A]

**Output:** Nurture follow-up message

**Tools needed:** CRM, email

---

#### 5c — Momentum (deal is warm, next step was agreed)

**Trigger:** Recent positive call or demo; a next step was agreed but not yet completed [A]

**Sequence:**
1. Verify next step is logged in CRM [A]
2. Confirm agreed timeline and who owns what [A]
3. Draft momentum message: recap what we agreed, what comes next, deliver any promised materials [A]
4. Set reminder for next touchpoint per agreed timeline [A]

**Output:** Momentum message + CRM reminder

**Tools needed:** CRM, email, calendar

---

## SECTION C — Calibration (User completes once at install)

These questions personalize the generic role spec to the specific rep.

| Question | Why it matters |
|----------|---------------|
| מה אתה מוכר ולמי? (product, ICP, industry) | Grounds all messaging in real context |
| איזה CRM אתה משתמש? | Required for connection |
| מה טווח המחירים? יש תבנית הצעה? | Methodology 4 can't run without it |
| תדביק מייל ישן שמייצג את הסגנון שלך | Voice/tone model — foundation of all drafts |
| מה מחזור הפולו-אפ הטבעי שלך (ימים בין נגיעות)? | Triggers for all follow-up methodologies |
| מאיפה מגיעים הלידים שלך בעיקר? (inbound / outbound / referrals) | Shapes Methodology 1 logic |
| מה אורך מחזור המכירה הטיפוסי? | Calibrates re-engagement vs. nurture timing |

---

## SECTION D — Template Usage Notes

This file is the replicable template for all role profiles. When running a new role through the pipeline:

1. Copy this file, rename to `[role]_role_profile_v1.md`
2. Run the 4 pillars for the new role archetype
3. Identify 3-5 core moments (Routines pillar → methodology candidates), ranked by frequency × value
4. For each moment, map: trigger → sequence → output → tools → day-one or needs-connection
5. Tag every claim [A] or [V]
6. Write calibration questions: what must the user tell the agent to make it theirs
7. Send to Elia for validation → lock

---

- v1 — Archetype build, all claims [A] unless marked otherwise
- Pending Elia validation
- Real interview data will upgrade [A] tags to [V] when available

**1. מכירות זה לא רק טלפון.** יש מימד פרונטלי מרכזי — פרזנטציות פנים-אל-פנים, בזום, או על קפה אצל הלקוח. זה רגע ליבה בפני עצמו.

**2. עולם ה"מה מציגים ואיך".** איך מציגים את המוצר/השירות ללקוח — בניית הפרזנטציה/הפיץ', התאמת המסר ללקוח הספציפי, מה שמים קדימה. זה לא קיים כרגע באפיון.

**3. הצעת מחיר היא גם פרונטלית.** לא רק מסמך שנשלח — הרבה פעמים מוצגת ומוסברת פנים-אל-פנים. המתודה צריכה לכלול הכנה להצגת ההצעה, לא רק ניסוח המסמך.

content.thinking:
Elia wants three main expansions to the sales profile:

1. **Presentation/pitch as a core methodology** — face-to-face, Zoom, or coffee meetings. This is a core moment in itself.
2. **The "what to present and how" world** — building the presentation/pitch, adapting the message to the specific customer, what to lead with.
3. **Proposal as also frontal** — often presented face-to-face, not just a document. The methodology needs to include preparation for presenting the proposal, not just drafting it.
4. **Maturation process + intelligent follow-up** — not just "lead went cold" but a full personalized maturation journey that leads the customer to closing. 

I'm thinking through how to structure this as new methodologies. The pitch/presentation build would be triggered when meeting a new prospect or scheduling a demo, pulling in account context about their pain points and role, then deciding whether to lead with the problem, product, or a case study based on where they are in the journey. From there I'd structure the narrative arc—problem to solution to proof to ask—and adapt the slides accordingly.

Then I'd prepare talking points tailored to their specific language and concerns, anticipate likely objections, and define the single clear ask for the end of the meeting. The output would be a customized presentation outline with talking points, using tools like Keynote, PowerPoint, or Canva along with the case library and CRM.

I'm also realizing the proposal presentation methodology needs to expand beyond just drafting the document—it should cover how to actually present it face-to-face or over Zoom, how to walk through the line items strategically, where to pause for questions, and what the follow-up looks like after the presentation to close the loop.

Beyond the transactional follow-up model, I'm thinking about this as a broader maturation journey where each customer has a personalized path forward. The agent tracks where they are in that journey, not just their CRM stage, and delivers contextual follow-ups that naturally move them forward—whether that's sharing relevant content at the right moment, addressing concerns that surfaced, or creating urgency organically. The three-type follow-up model still works at the micro level, but there's a macro orchestration happening above it that guides the entire maturation process.

I'm restructuring this around a customer journey framework with distinct stages—from cold and unaware, through engaged exploration, evaluation after a demo, decision-making after a proposal, and stalled situations that need a nudge. Each stage calls for a different follow-up approach, so the agent needs to understand where the customer actually sits in that progression.

I'm also thinking about how to integrate the tactical sub-types (5a/5b/5c) as specific moves within this larger journey intelligence, rather than treating them as standalone. And I want to expand the methodology list itself—pulling out pitch and presentation prep as its own full section, deepening the pricing methodology to include presentation strategy, and giving the follow-up section real substance around maturation and intelligent routing.

So the structure becomes six methodologies: initial outreach, pre-call prep, pitch and presentation building, post-call close, the full proposal cycle with presentation, and then the maturation journey with follow-up. For simpler implementations, I can note that just the first, second, fourth, and sixth are the essential spine.

**Version:** v2 — Archetype (pre-interview) — expanded per Elia feedback
**Author:** Alex (profiling agent)
**Status:** Pending Elia validation → lock

> **Tagging convention:**
> `[A]` = Analytical — derived from role archetype knowledge, sales methodology literature, standard B2B patterns
> `[V]` = Validated — heard directly in field interviews or confirmed by domain expert

> **Changes from v1:** Added Methodology 3 (Pitch/Presentation Build); expanded Methodology 5 (Proposal) to include frontal presentation prep; replaced mechanical follow-up 5a/5b/5c with full Maturation Journey model (Methodology 6). Updated Systems, Skills, Routines, and Calibration accordingly.

---

## SECTION A — Role Profile (4 Pillars)

### Pillar 1 — Role
- **Purpose:** Move prospects from first contact to signed deal. [A]
- **Success metric:** Pipeline conversion rate, deals closed (volume + value), quota attainment. [A]
- **Reports to:** Sales Manager / VP Sales. [A]
- **Who depends on them:** SDR who hands off leads, CS/onboarding who inherits the closed deal, management who reads pipeline health. [A]

---

### Pillar 2 — Routines (core moments, ranked by frequency × value)

| Rank | Moment | Frequency | Agent value |
|------|--------|-----------|-------------|
| 1 | מסע הבשלה והפולו-אפ | Daily | Highest — most reps are reactive; agent makes this proactive and personalized [A] |
| 2 | הכנה לשיחה | Per-meeting | High — skipped under time pressure, directly hurts call quality [A] |
| 3 | סיום שיחה | Per-meeting | Highest per-event — CRM lag + weak summaries are universal [A] |
| 4 | בניית פיץ'/פרזנטציה | Per-opportunity | High — most reps present generically; personalized pitch is a differentiator [A] |
| 5 | פנייה ראשונה | Weekly/per-lead | High — personalization takes long, generic openers underperform [A] |
| 6 | הצעת מחיר + הצגתה | Per-opportunity | High-stakes, less frequent; proposal presentation often underprepared [A] |

---

### Pillar 3 — Systems

| System | What reps do in it | Notes |
|--------|-------------------|-------|
| CRM (Salesforce / HubSpot / Pipedrive) | Log activities, update stages, view pipeline, set tasks | Most-used, most-complained-about. Often laggy or incomplete. [A] |
| Email (Gmail / Outlook) | Outreach, follow-ups, proposals | Primary async channel. [A] |
| Calendar (Google / Outlook) | Schedule calls, set reminders, see daily load | Trigger source for prep + follow-up. [A] |
| Presentation tool (Keynote / PowerPoint / Canva / Google Slides) | Build and adapt pitches and proposals for frontal delivery | Often one generic deck adapted per meeting — or not adapted at all. [A] |
| Case/content library (Drive / Notion / SharePoint) | Pull case studies, decks, pricing templates | Location varies by company; often ad-hoc. [A] |
| Messaging (WhatsApp / LinkedIn) | Outreach, informal follow-up | Increasingly primary in Israeli market. [A] |

**Calibration note:** CRM tool, presentation tool, case library location, and messaging preference must be confirmed per user at install.

---

### Pillar 4 — Skills

| Skill | Where it lives in workflow | Agent role |
|-------|--------------------------|------------|
| Discovery questioning | Methodology 2 (Pre-call Prep) | Prepare questions before call, not improvise during [A] |
| Pitch narrative construction | Methodology 3 (Pitch Build) | Decide what to lead with, structure the arc, cut what doesn't belong [A] |
| Objection handling | Methods 3 (pre-loaded), 4B (proposal presentation), 4 post-call (debrief) | Pre-load before presentation; debrief + draft written response after [A] |
| Champion enablement | Methodology 6, Stage 3 (Deciding) | Help internal contact make the case upward to their decision maker [A] |
| Funnel-stage awareness | All follow-up and maturation | Determines message type, tone, and timing per deal [A] |
| Follow-up cadence | Methodology 6 | Rep's personal rhythm; calibrated at install [A] |
| Quote/pricing structure | Methodology 5 | Needs rep's actual pricing template / tiers [A] |
| Voice/tone | All outbound messages | Learned from pasted past emails at install [A] |

---

## SECTION B — Agent Spec (6 Methodologies)

> **Minimum viable set** for a day-one agent: Methodologies 2, 4, 5, 6. Add 1 and 3 when rep wants proactive outreach support and presentation prep.

---

### Methodology 1 — פנייה ראשונה (First Outreach)

**Trigger:** New lead added to CRM / new contact identified for outreach [A]

**Sequence:**
1. Pull lead info — role, company, size, recent news if findable [A]
2. Identify likely pain point based on ICP and what rep is selling [A]
3. Match to one relevant case study or proof point [A]
4. Draft personalized opener in rep's voice — one clear value statement, one soft first ask (call, question, resource) [A]
5. Set follow-up reminder in CRM if no reply within rep's cadence [A]

**Output:** Draft first-touch message (email or WhatsApp) + CRM reminder

**Tools needed:** CRM, email/WhatsApp, case library

**Day-one or needs-connection:** Needs CRM connection + rep voice sample (paste at calibration)

---

### Methodology 2 — הכנה לשיחה (Pre-Call Prep)

**Trigger:** Meeting or call scheduled — calendar event created or CRM task set [A]

**Sequence:**
1. Pull account history from CRM — last interaction, open notes, current stage [A]
2. Check for recent news about the company or contact (new funding, product launch, leadership change) [A]
3. Review last call summary / email thread for open threads and promises made [A]
4. Generate discovery questions tailored to what's still unknown at this stage [A] ← *discovery questioning anchored here*
5. Pull 1-2 relevant case studies or proof points matched to known pain / industry [A]
6. Define call goal and the one ask at the end [A]

**Output:** Pre-call brief — account snapshot + open questions + relevant cases + call goal

**Tools needed:** CRM, calendar, case library, (optional: web search for news)

**Day-one or needs-connection:** CRM connection required; case library location confirmed at calibration

---

### Methodology 3 — בניית פיץ'/פרזנטציה (Pitch/Presentation Build) ⬅ NEW

**Trigger:** Meeting, demo, or frontal presentation scheduled — any context where rep presents rather than mainly listens [A]

**Sequence:**
1. Pull everything known about the customer: pain points surfaced so far, role, company size, likely decision criteria, what stage they're at [A]
2. Decide what to lead with: pain-first (open with their problem), outcome-first (open with the result they want), or proof-first (open with a case that mirrors them) — based on journey stage and what's already been said [A] ← *pitch narrative construction anchored here*
3. Structure the narrative arc: problem → why now → our approach → proof point → ROI framing → clear ask [A]
4. Adapt talking points to the customer's language and industry — replace generic claims with their context [A]
5. Decide what NOT to show — what to leave out so the meeting doesn't get lost in detail [A]
6. Pre-load objection responses for likely pushbacks based on what's surfaced so far [A] ← *objection handling anchored here (pre-loaded, not reactive)*
7. Define the one ask at the end of the meeting — what single next step is the rep walking out with? [A]

**Output:** Customized presentation outline + talking points + anticipated objections + the one ask

**Tools needed:** Presentation tool (Keynote/PowerPoint/Canva/Slides), case library, CRM

**Day-one or needs-connection:** Case library location confirmed at calibration; rep's presentation template needed

---

### Methodology 4 — סיום שיחה (Post-Call Close)

**Trigger:** Call or meeting ends [A]

**Sequence:**
1. Write structured call summary: what was said, what was revealed about pain/budget/authority/timeline, what was agreed [A]
2. Log to CRM: activity logged, stage updated, next task set [A]
3. Draft follow-up email: recap agreed next steps, attach any promised materials, clear CTA [A]
4. **If an objection came up:** debrief — identify the objection, draft a written response for inclusion in follow-up or future calls [A] ← *objection handling (reactive debrief) anchored here*
5. Pull matching case study if a specific concern surfaced [A]
6. Brief team if deal involves others [A]
7. Set next-step reminder [A]

**Output:** CRM log + follow-up email + objection response (when relevant) + internal brief (when relevant)

**Tools needed:** CRM, email, case library, messaging

**Day-one or needs-connection:** CRM connection + email connection required

---

### Methodology 5 — הצעת מחיר: ניסוח והצגה (Proposal — Full Cycle)

**Trigger:** Call summary contains positive signal or rep marks stage as proposal-ready [A]

**Two phases — document then presentation:**

**Phase A — ניסוח המסמך (drafting the proposal):**
1. Pull needs, constraints, and priorities from call summaries [A]
2. Apply to rep's pricing template / tiers [A]
3. Tailor framing — lead with the pain they named, connect to the right tier [A]
4. Suggest optional add-ons or alternative tiers if applicable [A]
5. Draft proposal cover note in rep's voice — warm, clear, low-friction next step [A]

**Phase B — הכנה להצגה פרונטלית (when proposal is presented, not just sent):** [A]
1. Decide what to walk through vs. leave for them to read — never read the document aloud [A]
2. Prepare a walk-through script for the 3 moments that matter most: scope, price, ROI — how to frame each one [A]
3. Pre-load price objection responses: anchor to value, offer tier alternatives, ask what their budget looks like [A] ← *objection handling (proposal-specific) anchored here*
4. Decide what's negotiable vs. not — and how to hold the line warmly [A]
5. Define the ask: what's the next step after they see the proposal? (sign / internal approval / call with manager?) [A]

**Output:** Proposal document + cover email + (when frontal) walk-through script + objection responses

**Tools needed:** Pricing template, email, presentation tool, CRM

**Day-one or needs-connection:** Pricing template required at calibration; email + CRM connection required

---

### Methodology 6 — מסע הבשלה והפולו-אפ (Maturation Journey & Follow-Up) ⬅ EXPANDED

**Core framing:** Follow-up is not a reaction to silence. It's a proactive, orchestrated sequence that moves each customer from where they are to where they need to be in order to decide. The agent maintains a living view of each open deal's position in the journey and routes the right message at the right moment.

**Trigger:** Daily — for each open deal, agent checks: last contact date, current stage, last interaction type, what was last promised [A]

---

**Journey Stages (how the agent tracks position):**

| Stage | Description | Primary goal |
|-------|-------------|--------------|
| 1 — Exploring | Customer responded, had at least one call, no proposal yet | Deepen relationship, surface pain more precisely |
| 2 — Evaluating | Demo or pitch delivered, customer is comparing options | Stay top of mind, build differentiation, reduce friction |
| 3 — Deciding | Proposal received, internal discussion happening | Support the internal champion, help them sell upward |
| 4 — Stalled | Was warm, now gone quiet (at any stage) | Re-engage with new value, not a repeat |
| 5 — Re-entry | Went cold, now re-engaged after a gap | Rebuild momentum with context; treat as a fresh start with history |

---

**Per-stage sequence:**

**Stage 1 — Exploring:**
1. Share relevant content (case study, insight, article) with a "made me think of you" framing — adds value, doesn't check in [A]
2. Follow rep's calibrated cadence for timing [A]
3. If a trigger event occurs (funding, new hire, press mention) — reach out immediately with a contextual note [A]

**Stage 2 — Evaluating:**
1. Send something that differentiates from likely alternatives — a proof point, a customer story that mirrors their situation, or a question that shows deeper understanding than competitors would ask [A]
2. Timing: 3-5 days after demo, then per cadence [A]
3. Avoid generic "just checking in" — every touch must add something [A]

**Stage 3 — Deciding:**
1. Draft a **champion enablement message** — something the internal contact can forward to their decision maker to make the case upward. This is the single highest-leverage action at this stage. [A] ← *champion enablement skill anchored here*
2. Keep it short, specific, and forward-able — the rep's contact should be able to paste it into an internal email [A]
3. If no reply in [X] days: send a soft low-friction check-in — "Is there anything that would help move this forward?" [A]

**Stage 4 — Stalled:**
1. Find a new angle before reaching out — news hook, relevant case, change in their situation — so the message feels like a gift, not a chase [A]
2. Do NOT repeat the last message with different words [A]
3. Two attempts with no reply → flag as dormant, suggest pipeline cleanup [A]

**Stage 5 — Re-entry:**
1. Acknowledge the gap warmly without apologizing for it [A]
2. Reference what's changed — on rep's side (new case, updated offer) or theirs (company news) — to justify reconnecting [A]
3. Soft ask to reconnect, no pressure [A]

---

**Output:** Daily prioritized follow-up list — which deals need a touch today, which stage they're in, suggested message per deal + champion enablement draft (when at Stage 3)

**Tools needed:** CRM, email, WhatsApp, case library, calendar

**Day-one or needs-connection:** CRM connection required; email/WhatsApp connection required

---

| מה אתה מוכר ולמי? (product, ICP, industry) | Grounds all messaging in real context |

| מה ההתנגדויות הנפוצות שאתה שומע לפני סגירה? | Pre-loads objection responses in Methodologies 3 and 5B |

1. Copy this file, rename to `[role]_role_profile_v1.md`
2. Apply the 4 pillars to the new role archetype

2. Decide what to lead with: pain-first (open with their problem), outcome-first (open with the result they want), or proof-first (open with a case that mirrors them) — based on journey stage and what's already been said [A] ← *pitch narrative construction anchored here*
3. Structure the narrative arc: problem → why now → our approach → proof point → ROI framing → clear ask [A]
4. Adapt talking points to the customer's language and industry — replace generic claims with their context [A]
5. Decide what NOT to show — what to leave out so the meeting doesn't get lost in detail [A]
6. Pre-load objection responses for likely pushbacks based on what's surfaced so far [A] ← *objection handling anchored here (pre-loaded, not reactive)*
7. Define the one ask at the end of the meeting — what single next step is the rep walking out with? [A]

**Output:** Customized presentation outline + talking points + anticipated objections + the one ask

**Tools needed:** Presentation tool (Keynote/PowerPoint/Canva/Slides), case library, CRM

**Day-one or needs-connection:** Case library location confirmed at calibration; rep's presentation template needed

---

### Methodology 4 — סיום שיחה (Post-Call Close)

**Trigger:** Call or meeting ends [A]

**Sequence:**
1. Write structured call summary: what was said, what was revealed about pain/budget/authority/timeline, what was agreed [A]
2. Log to CRM: activity logged, stage updated, next task set [A]
3. Draft follow-up email: recap agreed next steps, attach any promised materials, clear CTA [A]
4. **If an objection came up:** debrief — identify the objection, draft a written response for inclusion in follow-up or future calls [A] ← *objection handling (reactive debrief) anchored here*
5. Pull matching case study if a specific concern surfaced [A]
6. Brief team if deal involves others [A]
7. Set next-step reminder [A]

**Output:** CRM log + follow-up email + objection response (when relevant) + internal brief (when relevant)

**Tools needed:** CRM, email, case library, messaging

**Day-one or needs-connection:** CRM connection + email connection required

---

### Methodology 5 — הצעת מחיר: ניסוח והצגה (Proposal — Full Cycle)

**Trigger:** Call summary contains positive signal or rep marks stage as proposal-ready [A]

**Two phases — document then presentation:**

**Phase A — ניסוח המסמך (drafting the proposal):**
1. Pull needs, constraints, and priorities from call summaries [A]
2. Apply to rep's pricing template / tiers [A]
3. Tailor framing — lead with the pain they named, connect to the right tier [A]
4. Suggest optional add-ons or alternative tiers if applicable [A]
5. Draft proposal cover note in rep's voice — warm, clear, low-friction next step [A]

**Phase B — הכנה להצגה פרונטלית (when proposal is presented, not just sent):** [A]
1. Decide what to walk through vs. leave for them to read — never read the document aloud [A]
2. Prepare a walk-through script for the 3 moments that matter most: scope, price, ROI — how to frame each one [A]
3. Pre-load price objection responses: anchor to value, offer tier alternatives, ask what their budget looks like [A] ← *objection handling (proposal-specific) anchored here*
4. Decide what's negotiable vs. not — and how to hold the line warmly [A]
5. Define the ask: what's the next step after they see the proposal? (sign / internal approval / call with manager?) [A]

**Output:** Proposal document + cover email + (when frontal) walk-through script + objection responses

**Tools needed:** Pricing template, email, presentation tool, CRM

**Day-one or needs-connection:** Pricing template required at calibration; email + CRM connection required

---

### Methodology 6 — מסע הבשלה והפולו-אפ (Maturation Journey & Follow-Up) ⬅ EXPANDED

**Core framing:** Follow-up is not a reaction to silence. It's a proactive, orchestrated sequence that moves each customer from where they are to where they need to be in order to decide. The agent maintains a living view of each open deal's position in the journey and routes the right message at the right moment.

**Trigger:** Daily — for each open deal, agent checks: last contact date, current stage, last interaction type, what was last promised [A]

---

**Journey Stages (how the agent tracks position):**

| Stage | Description | Primary goal |
|-------|-------------|--------------|
| 1 — Exploring | Customer responded, had at least one call, no proposal yet | Deepen relationship, surface pain more precisely |
| 2 — Evaluating | Demo or pitch delivered, customer is comparing options | Stay top of mind, build differentiation, reduce friction |
| 3 — Deciding | Proposal received, internal discussion happening | Support the internal champion, help them sell upward |
| 4 — Stalled | Was warm, now gone quiet (at any stage) | Re-engage with new value, not a repeat |
| 5 — Re-entry | Went cold, now re-engaged after a gap | Rebuild momentum with context; treat as a fresh start with history |

---

**Per-stage sequence:**

**Stage 1 — Exploring:**
1. Share relevant content (case study, insight, article) with a "made me think of you" framing — adds value, doesn't check in [A]
2. Follow rep's calibrated cadence for timing [A]
3. If a trigger event occurs (funding, new hire, press mention) — reach out immediately with a contextual note [A]

**Stage 2 — Evaluating:**
1. Send something that differentiates from likely alternatives — a proof point, a customer story that mirrors their situation, or a question that shows deeper understanding than competitors would ask [A]
2. Timing: 3-5 days after demo, then per cadence [A]
3. Avoid generic "just checking in" — every touch must add something [A]

**Stage 3 — Deciding:**
1. Draft a **champion enablement message** — something the internal contact can forward to their decision maker to make the case upward. This is the single highest-leverage action at this stage. [A] ← *champion enablement skill anchored here*
2. Keep it short, specific, and forward-able — the rep's contact should be able to paste it into an internal email [A]
3. If no reply in [X] days: send a soft low-friction check-in — "Is there anything that would help move this forward?" [A]

**Stage 4 — Stalled:**
1. Find a new angle before reaching out — news hook, relevant case, change in their situation — so the message feels like a gift, not a chase [A]
2. Do NOT repeat the last message with different words [A]
3. Two attempts with no reply → flag as dormant, suggest pipeline cleanup [A]

**Stage 5 — Re-entry:**
1. Acknowledge the gap warmly without apologizing for it [A]
2. Reference what's changed — on rep's side (new case, updated offer) or theirs (company news) — to justify reconnecting [A]
3. Soft ask to reconnect, no pressure [A]

---

**Output:** Daily prioritized follow-up list — which deals need a touch today, which stage they're in, suggested message per deal + champion enablement draft (when at Stage 3)

**Tools needed:** CRM, email, WhatsApp, case library, calendar

**Day-one or needs-connection:** CRM connection required; email/WhatsApp connection required

---

## SECTION C — Calibration (User completes once at install)

| Question | Why it matters |
|----------|---------------|
| מה אתה מוכר ולמי? (product, ICP, industry) | Grounds all messaging in real context |
| איזה CRM אתה משתמש? | Required for connection |
| מה טווח המחירים? יש תבנית הצעה? | Methodology 5 can't run without it |
| תדביק מייל ישן שמייצג את הסגנון שלך | Voice/tone model — foundation of all drafts |
| מה מחזור הפולו-אפ הטבעי שלך (ימים בין נגיעות)? | Triggers for Methodology 6 cadence |
| מאיפה מגיעים הלידים שלך בעיקר? (inbound / outbound / referrals) | Shapes Methodology 1 logic |
| מה אורך מחזור המכירה הטיפוסי? | Calibrates stage timing and re-engagement thresholds |
| מה ההתנגדויות הנפוצות שאתה שומע לפני סגירה? | Pre-loads objection responses in Methodologies 3 and 5B |

---

## SECTION D — Template Usage Notes

This file is the replicable template for all role profiles. When running a new role:

1. Copy this file, rename to `[role]_role_profile_v1.md`
2. Apply the 4 pillars to the new role archetype
3. Identify 4-6 core moments (Routines pillar → methodology candidates), ranked by frequency × value
4. For each moment: trigger → sequence → output → tools → day-one or needs-connection
5. Tag every claim `[A]` or `[V]`
6. Anchor skills explicitly to the methodology steps where they belong
7. Write calibration questions — what must the user tell the agent to make it theirs
8. Note the minimum viable subset of methodologies for a day-one agent
9. Send to Elia for validation → lock

---

- v2 — Archetype build, expanded per Elia feedback (presentation dimension, frontal proposal, maturation journey)
- All claims `[A]` unless marked otherwise

- Real interview data will upgrade `[A]` tags to `[V]` when available

content.thinking:
Elia's feedback is really insightful. He's saying Methodology 6 is too rigid — it's a fixed script per stage, not a thinking framework. The agent should know HOW to think about maturation, not WHAT to do at each predefined step.

Let me think about:
1. How to rewrite Methodology 6 as a "thinking scaffold" not a script
2. Answer the question about whether the other 5 methodologies need the same treatment

**On the question about other methodologies:**

This is a good distinction to think through. Let me consider each:
Methodology 1 is pretty solid as a template — the research-to-outreach sequence is fairly universal, and what varies is just the product knowledge and customer fit, which the calibration handles. Methodology 2 works similarly; the pre-call prep ritual is standard across most situations, and the variables are just what information goes into the brief based on what's known about the prospect. The sequence itself doesn't need to be a thinking framework.

Methodology 3 is where there's actual variation — deciding what to lead with (pain, outcome, or proof) really does depend on the customer and product type. The thinking framework is already embedded in step 2, so the sequence is a good scaffold, though I could make step 2 more explicit as a judgment call rather than a default.

Methodology 4 is quite universal — structured summary, CRM log, follow-up email, objection debrief — with very little variation needed. Methodology 5 (the proposal cycle) has phase A fairly template-based and phase B with judgment calls already baked in, so mostly fine. Methodology 6 is where the real variation kicks in.

The sales cycle itself varies wildly depending on the product and buyer — SaaS might move in a month while enterprise takes six, some deals are solo decisions and others require committees, some customers prefer WhatsApp and others want formal email. A fixed five-stage script is too rigid for that kind of open-ended, irregular journey. The key insight is that the other five methodologies are event-driven with clear triggers and mostly universal actions, whereas Methodology 6 is ongoing and needs a thinking framework instead of a script. That said, I should add a note that the quality of execution in those other methodologies matters more than just following the sequence.

For Methodology 6, the shift is to move away from "if Stage X then do Y" and instead have the agent diagnose where the customer actually is by reading signals, infer what's blocking them, decide what kind of move would work for this specific customer, choose the right channel and timing, then execute. The five-stage model becomes diagnostic vocabulary for naming where a customer sits rather than a rigid script to follow.

I also need to capture the maturation profile of the product or service — the typical sales cycle length, how many people are usually involved in the decision, and what typically causes deals to stall.

I should also ask about preferred customer channels and whether decisions are one-time, annual, or recurring, since that shapes the urgency and approach.

Now I'm structuring the full Methodology 6 response with the core principle first, then the diagnostic layer using the five stages as vocabulary, the judgment questions an agent works through, the channel and timing logic, and finally how to describe the output.

The key distinction is that the other five methodologies are event-triggered with fairly universal sequences—the variation comes from what content fills those sequences, not the structure itself. Only Methodology 6 requires a rewrite because it's an ongoing judgment process rather than event-driven. I could make the judgment calls more explicit across the other methodologies too, but that's refinement rather than structural change.

I'll write v3 now, keeping the other methodologies intact and rewriting only Methodology 6, while updating the Calibration section to reflect how the product matures over time.

### Methodology 2 — הכנה לשיחה (Pre-Call Prep)

**Trigger:** Meeting/call scheduled — calendar event created or CRM task set [A]

**Sequence:**
1. Pull account history from CRM — last interaction, open notes, current stage [A]
2. Check for recent news about the company or contact [A]
3. Review last call summary / email thread for open threads and promises made [A]
4. Generate discovery questions tailored to what's still unknown at this stage [A] ← *discovery questioning anchored here*
5. Pull 1-2 relevant cases matched to known pain / industry [A]

**Tools needed:** CRM, calendar, case library, (optional: web search)

### Methodology 3 — בניית פיץ'/פרזנטציה (Pitch/Presentation Build)

**Trigger:** Meeting or demo scheduled where rep presents rather than mainly listens [A]

**Sequence:**
1. Pull everything known about the customer: pain surfaced so far, role, company size, decision criteria, journey stage [A]
2. Decide what to lead with — pain-first / outcome-first / proof-first — based on what's been said and where they are [A] ← *pitch narrative construction anchored here*
3. Structure the narrative arc: problem → why now → approach → proof → ROI → ask [A]
4. Adapt talking points to the customer's language and context — remove generic claims [A]
5. Decide what NOT to show — leave out what doesn't serve the meeting goal [A]
6. Pre-load objection responses for likely pushbacks based on what's surfaced [A] ← *objection handling pre-loaded here*
7. Define the one ask: what single next step is the rep walking out with? [A]

**Output:** Presentation outline + talking points + anticipated objections + the one ask

**Tools needed:** Presentation tool, case library, CRM

**Day-one or needs-connection:** Case library and presentation template confirmed at calibration

---

### Methodology 4 — סיום שיחה (Post-Call Close)

**Trigger:** Call or meeting ends [A]

**Sequence:**
1. Write structured call summary: what was said, what was revealed (pain/budget/authority/timeline), what was agreed [A]
2. Log to CRM: activity logged, stage updated, next task set [A]
3. Draft follow-up email: recap agreed next steps, attach promised materials, clear CTA [A]
4. **If an objection came up:** debrief — identify it, draft written response for follow-up or future calls [A] ← *objection handling (reactive debrief) anchored here*
5. Pull matching case study if a specific concern surfaced [A]
6. Brief team if deal involves others [A]
7. Set next-step reminder [A]

**Output:** CRM log + follow-up email + objection response (when relevant) + internal brief (when relevant)

**Tools needed:** CRM, email, case library, messaging

**Day-one or needs-connection:** CRM + email connection required

---

### Methodology 5 — הצעת מחיר: ניסוח והצגה (Proposal — Full Cycle)

**Trigger:** Call summary contains positive signal or rep marks stage as proposal-ready [A]

**Phase A — ניסוח המסמך:**
1. Pull needs, constraints, priorities from call summaries [A]
2. Apply to rep's pricing template / tiers [A]
3. Tailor framing — lead with their stated pain, connect to the right tier [A]
4. Suggest optional add-ons or alternative tiers if applicable [A]
5. Draft proposal cover note in rep's voice [A]

**Phase B — הכנה להצגה פרונטלית (when proposal is presented, not just sent):**
1. Decide what to walk through vs. leave for them to read — never read the document aloud [A]
2. Prepare walk-through script for the 3 moments that matter most: scope, price, ROI [A]
3. Pre-load price objection responses: anchor to value, offer tier alternatives, ask about budget [A] ← *objection handling (proposal-specific) anchored here*
4. Decide what's negotiable vs. not — how to hold the line warmly [A]
5. Define the ask: next step after they see the proposal [A]

**Output:** Proposal document + cover email + (when frontal) walk-through script + objection responses

**Tools needed:** Pricing template, email, presentation tool, CRM

**Day-one or needs-connection:** Pricing template required at calibration; email + CRM connection required

---

### Methodology 6 — מסע הבשלה והפולו-אפ (Maturation Journey & Follow-Up) ⬅ REWRITTEN

**Core principle:** Every product has a different maturation process. Every customer has a different maturation process. This methodology does not prescribe what to do — it gives the agent a thinking framework to diagnose each deal individually and decide what move makes sense for that specific customer at that specific moment. [A]

**Trigger:** Daily review — the agent scans all open deals, identifies which need a touch, and determines what kind of touch is right for each. [A]

---

#### Layer 1 — Diagnostic vocabulary (where is this customer?)

The five states below are diagnostic language — not a pipeline script. A customer can be in any state, skip states, move backwards, or sit in the same state for months. The agent uses these to name where someone is, not to trigger a fixed action.

| State | What it means | Key signal |
|-------|--------------|------------|
| **Exploring** | Engaged, interested, no real stakes yet — learning, not deciding | Positive but no urgency; asks general questions |
| **Evaluating** | Actively comparing options; stakes are real | Asking about specifics, competitors, or timelines |
| **Deciding** | A real proposal or decision is on the table internally | Internally discussing; referencing "we" and timelines |
| **Stalled** | Was warmer, now quiet — reason unknown | Gone dark after positive momentum |
| **Re-entry** | Came back after going cold | Re-initiated contact after a gap |

The agent diagnoses state by reading: last interaction content, CRM history, tone of last exchange, days since contact, and any context about what the customer's internal situation looks like. [A]

---

#### Layer 2 — Judgment questions (what would move this specific customer?)

For each deal that needs a touch, the agent works through:

1. **Where are they in their own process?** Not just "what CRM stage" — what's actually happening on their side right now? Are they in budget season? Distracted? Comparing vendors? [A]

2. **What's the real blocker?** Is it timing, budget, internal alignment, skepticism, competing priorities, or just friction? Different blockers need different moves. [A]

3. **What would feel like value to them right now, not to me?** A follow-up that serves the rep's anxiety is noise. A follow-up that answers a question they're probably sitting with is a gift. [A]

4. **What's the one thing that would move them to the next state?** Sometimes it's a case study. Sometimes it's a question that surfaces the unspoken concern. Sometimes it's silence. [A]

5. **Is this deal still worth pursuing?** If signals suggest the customer has moved on internally, flag it — don't keep nurturing a dead deal. [A]

---

#### Layer 3 — Channel and timing logic

**Channel selection** — not preference, but context: [A]

| Signal | Right channel |
|--------|--------------|
| Relationship is warm and informal | WhatsApp — feels human, not sales-y |
| Content/materials to share | Email — scannable, forwardable |
| Complex or sensitive message | Email — gives them time to process |
| Urgent or time-sensitive | WhatsApp or phone |
| First contact with new stakeholder | Email — professional default |
| Re-entry after a gap | WhatsApp if relationship existed; email if not |

**Timing logic** — calibrated at install per rep's product/cycle: [A]
- Not based on fixed intervals but on: what was last promised, what their internal calendar likely looks like, how long this customer's buying process typically takes
- If a trigger event occurs (their company news, end of quarter, re-opened conversation) — that overrides cadence; reach out immediately
- If no natural trigger: use the rep's calibrated follow-up rhythm as a default floor

**Special case — Deciding stage:**
When a customer is in the Deciding state, the most effective move is often not a follow-up to the rep — it's enabling the internal champion. Draft something the internal contact can forward to their decision-maker that makes the case without the rep being in the room. Short, specific, forward-able. [A]

---

**Output:** Daily prioritized list — which deals need a touch, diagnosed state, the specific judgment call for each, and a suggested message or action (not a template — tailored to that customer based on the above)

**Tools needed:** CRM, email, WhatsApp, case library, calendar

**Day-one or needs-connection:** CRM + email/WhatsApp connection required

---

## SECTION C — Calibration (User completes once at install)

Two layers: **who the rep is** (voice, product, ICP) and **how their product matures** (the input M6 needs to build the right journey per customer).

**Layer 1 — Rep profile (universal across all methodologies):**

| Question | Why it matters |
|----------|---------------|
| מה אתה מוכר ולמי? (product, ICP, industry) | Grounds all messaging in real context |
| איזה CRM אתה משתמש? | Required for connection |
| מה טווח המחירים? יש תבנית הצעה? | Methodology 5 can't run without it |
| תדביק מייל ישן שמייצג את הסגנון שלך | Voice/tone model — foundation of all drafts |
| מה ההתנגדויות הנפוצות שאתה שומע לפני סגירה? | Pre-loads objection responses in M3 and M5B |
| מאיפה מגיעים הלידים שלך? (inbound / outbound / referrals) | Shapes M1 logic |

**Layer 2 — Maturation profile (input for Methodology 6):**

| Question | Why it matters for M6 |
|----------|----------------------|
| מה אורך מחזור המכירה הטיפוסי? | Calibrates when a deal is "stalled" vs. just slow |
| כמה אנשים מעורבים בדרך כלל בהחלטה? | Solo decision vs. committee changes the whole journey — especially champion enablement |
| מה בדרך כלל גורם לעסקה להיתקע? | Pre-loads the agent's blocker-diagnosis; it knows what to look for |
| מה הערוצים המועדפים אצל הלקוחות שלך? (מייל / וואטסאפ / שיחה) | Sets the channel-selection defaults for this rep's world |
| מה מחזור הפולו-אפ הטבעי שלך? (ימים בין נגיעות) | Default floor cadence when no better signal exists |
| מה סוג ההחלטה — רכישה חד-פעמית / מינוי / חידוש שנתי? | Shapes urgency logic and re-entry framing |

---

## SECTION D — Template Usage Notes

This file is the replicable template for all role profiles. When running a new role:

1. Copy this file, rename to `[role]_role_profile_v1.md`
2. Apply the 4 pillars to the new role archetype
3. Identify 4-6 core moments (Routines pillar → methodology candidates), ranked by frequency × value
4. For each event-triggered moment (call ends, meeting scheduled, proposal ready): write a sequence — these are universal enough to prescribe
5. For any ongoing, open-ended process (equivalent to maturation in sales): write a thinking framework — diagnose / judge / choose — not a script
6. Tag every claim `[A]` or `[V]`
7. Split calibration into: rep/role profile (universal) + process profile (role-specific, feeds the framework methodologies)
8. Note the minimum viable methodology subset for a day-one agent
9. Send to Elia for validation → lock

---

## STATUS
- v3 — M6 rewritten as thinking framework per Elia feedback; calibration split into rep profile + maturation profile
- All claims `[A]` unless marked otherwise
- Pending Elia validation
- Real interview data will upgrade `[A]` tags to `[V]` when available

6. Pre-load objection responses for likely pushbacks based on what's surfaced [A] ← *objection handling pre-loaded here*
7. Define the one ask: what single next step is the rep walking out with? [A]

**Output:** Presentation outline + talking points + anticipated objections + the one ask

**Tools needed:** Presentation tool, case library, CRM

**Day-one or needs-connection:** Case library and presentation template confirmed at calibration

---

### Methodology 4 — סיום שיחה (Post-Call Close)

**Trigger:** Call or meeting ends [A]

**Sequence:**
1. Write structured call summary: what was said, what was revealed (pain/budget/authority/timeline), what was agreed [A]
2. Log to CRM: activity logged, stage updated, next task set [A]
3. Draft follow-up email: recap agreed next steps, attach promised materials, clear CTA [A]
4. **If an objection came up:** debrief — identify it, draft written response for follow-up or future calls [A] ← *objection handling (reactive debrief) anchored here*
5. Pull matching case study if a specific concern surfaced [A]
6. Brief team if deal involves others [A]
7. Set next-step reminder [A]

**Output:** CRM log + follow-up email + objection response (when relevant) + internal brief (when relevant)

**Tools needed:** CRM, email, case library, messaging

**Day-one or needs-connection:** CRM + email connection required

---

### Methodology 5 — הצעת מחיר: ניסוח והצגה (Proposal — Full Cycle)

**Trigger:** Call summary contains positive signal or rep marks stage as proposal-ready [A]

**Phase A — ניסוח המסמך:**
1. Pull needs, constraints, priorities from call summaries [A]
2. Apply to rep's pricing template / tiers [A]
3. Tailor framing — lead with their stated pain, connect to the right tier [A]
4. Suggest optional add-ons or alternative tiers if applicable [A]
5. Draft proposal cover note in rep's voice [A]

**Phase B — הכנה להצגה פרונטלית (when proposal is presented, not just sent):**
1. Decide what to walk through vs. leave for them to read — never read the document aloud [A]
2. Prepare walk-through script for the 3 moments that matter most: scope, price, ROI [A]
3. Pre-load price objection responses: anchor to value, offer tier alternatives, ask about budget [A] ← *objection handling (proposal-specific) anchored here*
4. Decide what's negotiable vs. not — how to hold the line warmly [A]
5. Define the ask: next step after they see the proposal [A]

**Output:** Proposal document + cover email + (when frontal) walk-through script + objection responses

**Tools needed:** Pricing template, email, presentation tool, CRM

**Day-one or needs-connection:** Pricing template required at calibration; email + CRM connection required

---

### Methodology 6 — מסע הבשלה והפולו-אפ (Maturation Journey & Follow-Up) ⬅ REWRITTEN

**Core principle:** Every product has a different maturation process. Every customer has a different maturation process. This methodology does not prescribe what to do — it gives the agent a thinking framework to diagnose each deal individually and decide what move makes sense for that specific customer at that specific moment. [A]

**Trigger:** Daily review — the agent scans all open deals, identifies which need a touch, and determines what kind of touch is right for each. [A]

---

#### Layer 1 — Diagnostic vocabulary (where is this customer?)

The five states below are diagnostic language — not a pipeline script. A customer can be in any state, skip states, move backwards, or sit in the same state for months. The agent uses these to name where someone is, not to trigger a fixed action.

| State | What it means | Key signal |
|-------|--------------|------------|
| **Exploring** | Engaged, interested, no real stakes yet — learning, not deciding | Positive but no urgency; asks general questions |
| **Evaluating** | Actively comparing options; stakes are real | Asking about specifics, competitors, or timelines |
| **Deciding** | A real proposal or decision is on the table internally | Internally discussing; referencing "we" and timelines |
| **Stalled** | Was warmer, now quiet — reason unknown | Gone dark after positive momentum |
| **Re-entry** | Came back after going cold | Re-initiated contact after a gap |

The agent diagnoses state by reading: last interaction content, CRM history, tone of last exchange, days since contact, and any context about what the customer's internal situation looks like. [A]

---

#### Layer 2 — Judgment questions (what would move this specific customer?)

For each deal that needs a touch, the agent works through:

1. **Where are they in their own process?** Not just "what CRM stage" — what's actually happening on their side right now? Are they in budget season? Distracted? Comparing vendors? [A]

2. **What's the real blocker?** Is it timing, budget, internal alignment, skepticism, competing priorities, or just friction? Different blockers need different moves. [A]

3. **What would feel like value to them right now, not to me?** A follow-up that serves the rep's anxiety is noise. A follow-up that answers a question they're probably sitting with is a gift. [A]

4. **What's the one thing that would move them to the next state?** Sometimes it's a case study. Sometimes it's a question that surfaces the unspoken concern. Sometimes it's silence. [A]

5. **Is this deal still worth pursuing?** If signals suggest the customer has moved on internally, flag it — don't keep nurturing a dead deal. [A]

---

#### Layer 3 — Channel and timing logic

**Channel selection** — not preference, but context: [A]

| Signal | Right channel |
|--------|--------------|
| Relationship is warm and informal | WhatsApp — feels human, not sales-y |
| Content/materials to share | Email — scannable, forwardable |
| Complex or sensitive message | Email — gives them time to process |
| Urgent or time-sensitive | WhatsApp or phone |
| First contact with new stakeholder | Email — professional default |
| Re-entry after a gap | WhatsApp if relationship existed; email if not |

**Timing logic** — calibrated at install per rep's product/cycle: [A]
- Not based on fixed intervals but on: what was last promised, what their internal calendar likely looks like, how long this customer's buying process typically takes
- If a trigger event occurs (their company news, end of quarter, re-opened conversation) — that overrides cadence; reach out immediately
- If no natural trigger: use the rep's calibrated follow-up rhythm as a default floor

**Special case — Deciding stage:**
When a customer is in the Deciding state, the most effective move is often not a follow-up to the rep — it's enabling the internal champion. Draft something the internal contact can forward to their decision-maker that makes the case without the rep being in the room. Short, specific, forward-able. [A]

---

**Output:** Daily prioritized list — which deals need a touch, diagnosed state, the specific judgment call for each, and a suggested message or action (not a template — tailored to that customer based on the above)

**Tools needed:** CRM, email, WhatsApp, case library, calendar

**Day-one or needs-connection:** CRM + email/WhatsApp connection required

---

## SECTION C — Calibration (User completes once at install)

Two layers: **who the rep is** (voice, product, ICP) and **how their product matures** (the input M6 needs to build the right journey per customer).

**Layer 1 — Rep profile (universal across all methodologies):**

| Question | Why it matters |
|----------|---------------|
| מה אתה מוכר ולמי? (product, ICP, industry) | Grounds all messaging in real context |
| איזה CRM אתה משתמש? | Required for connection |
| מה טווח המחירים? יש תבנית הצעה? | Methodology 5 can't run without it |
| תדביק מייל ישן שמייצג את הסגנון שלך | Voice/tone model — foundation of all drafts |
| מה ההתנגדויות הנפוצות שאתה שומע לפני סגירה? | Pre-loads objection responses in M3 and M5B |
| מאיפה מגיעים הלידים שלך? (inbound / outbound / referrals) | Shapes M1 logic |

**Layer 2 — Maturation profile (input for Methodology 6):**

| Question | Why it matters for M6 |
|----------|----------------------|
| מה אורך מחזור המכירה הטיפוסי? | Calibrates when a deal is "stalled" vs. just slow |
| כמה אנשים מעורבים בדרך כלל בהחלטה? | Solo decision vs. committee changes the whole journey — especially champion enablement |
| מה בדרך כלל גורם לעסקה להיתקע? | Pre-loads the agent's blocker-diagnosis; it knows what to look for |
| מה הערוצים המועדפים אצל הלקוחות שלך? (מייל / וואטסאפ / שיחה) | Sets the channel-selection defaults for this rep's world |
| מה מחזור הפולו-אפ הטבעי שלך? (ימים בין נגיעות) | Default floor cadence when no better signal exists |
| מה סוג ההחלטה — רכישה חד-פעמית / מינוי / חידוש שנתי? | Shapes urgency logic and re-entry framing |

---

## SECTION D — Template Usage Notes

This file is the replicable template for all role profiles. When running a new role:

1. Copy this file, rename to `[role]_role_profile_v1.md`
2. Apply the 4 pillars to the new role archetype
3. Identify 4-6 core moments (Routines pillar → methodology candidates), ranked by frequency × value
4. For each event-triggered moment (call ends, meeting scheduled, proposal ready): write a sequence — these are universal enough to prescribe
5. For any ongoing, open-ended process (equivalent to maturation in sales): write a thinking framework — diagnose / judge / choose — not a script
6. Tag every claim `[A]` or `[V]`
7. Split calibration into: rep/role profile (universal) + process profile (role-specific, feeds the framework methodologies)
8. Note the minimum viable methodology subset for a day-one agent
9. Send to Elia for validation → lock

---

## STATUS
- v3 — M6 rewritten as thinking framework per Elia feedback; calibration split into rep profile + maturation profile
- All claims `[A]` unless marked otherwise
- Pending Elia validation
- Real interview data will upgrade `[A]` tags to `[V]` when available

**ההבחנה לתבנית (Section D):**
הוספתי כלל כללי ל-Section D: כשמגיעים לתפקיד חדש — מתודות event-triggered → כותבים רצף. מתודות תהליכיות-מתמשכות → כותבים framework (diagnose / judge / choose). ההבחנה הזו עובדת לכל תפקיד.

- Layer 1: פרופיל המוכר (כלים, קול, מוצר) — אוניברסלי לכל המתודות
- Layer 2: **פרופיל ההבשלה** (חדש) — מה אורך מחזור המכירה, כמה אנשים מחליטים, מה גורם לתקיעות, איזה ערוץ מועדף — ה-input שM6 צריכה כדי לבנות את המסע הנכון לכל לקוח

content.thinking:
Now I need to write the "paste block" — the text a user pastes to their NanoClaw agent after installation that teaches it the sales profession. 

Key requirements:
- Hebrew first, second person (to the agent)
- Tone: human, not robotic
- No em-dashes
- MVP day-one = Methodologies 2, 4, 5, 6 as core; 1+3 as optional add-on marked clearly
- Structure:
  1. Opening — addressing the agent in second person
  2. Each methodology — trigger → sequence the agent runs → what it returns
  3. M6 — thinking instructions, not a sequence (5 diagnostic states + channel logic + 5 judgment questions)
  4. Calibration — user fills in their info inline as part of the paste block

The paste block should feel like a briefing to an assistant, not a technical spec. Once pasted, the agent instantly understands its role and how to operate as a sales assistant.

I'll structure it with an opening paragraph establishing who the agent is and what it does, then a calibration section where the user fills in their details before pasting — things like what they're selling, who they're selling to, and their CRM system. This way the block is already personalized when deployed.

For the event-triggered methodologies, I'll use clear language like "when a meeting gets scheduled for me" or "when you tell me a meeting is set," followed by numbered steps and a "what you return to me" section. For M6, the daily pipeline scan will follow a similar pattern with explicit triggers and outputs.

I'm also thinking about whether to have the calibration questions embedded at the start of the agent's conversation or presented as a pre-paste form — the conversational approach might feel more natural and engaging, though the form approach is more efficient. I need to structure the full agent prompt in Hebrew, making sure to use the user's details as context for each workflow step, and avoiding em-dashes in favor of colons and line breaks for clarity. ערוץ מועדף: [העתק מחלק A]
מרווח פולו-אפ: [העתק מחלק A]

אתה עוזר המכירות שלי. אתה מכיר את תהליכי העבודה המקצועיים שמפורטים כאן. כשאתאר לך מצב, תריץ את התהליך המתאים. השתמש תמיד בפרטים שמסרתי לך למעלה, כדי שמה שתייצר יהיה שלי ולא גנרי.

---

### תהליך 1: הכנה לפגישה

כשאני אומר לך שנקבעה לי פגישה עם לקוח:

שאל אותי: עם מי, באיזה שלב הם, ומה ידוע לך עליהם עד כה.

אז הכן לי תדריך קצר שכולל:
- מה קרה בשיחות קודמות (אם יש) ומה נשאר פתוח
- שאלות שיפתחו אותם לפי מה שעדיין לא ידוע לי על הצורך שלהם
- קייס אחד או שניים שרלוונטיים למה שאני יודע עליהם
- מה המטרה שלי בפגישה הזו ומה אני רוצה לצאת ממנה עם יד

תחזיר לי: סיכום קצר, מוכן לקריאה חמש דקות לפני שאני נכנס.

---

### תהליך 2: סיום שיחה

כשאני אומר לך שנגמרה לי שיחה עם לקוח:

שאל אותי: מה עבר בשיחה, מה גילינו, מה הסכמנו עליו, ואם עלתה התנגדות, מה היתה.

אז כתוב לי:
- סיכום מובנה לCRM: מה נאמר, מה התגלה, מה הסוכן הבא
- טיוטת מייל המשך: מסכם מה הסכמנו, מצרף מה שהבטחתי, CTA אחד ברור
- אם עלתה התנגדות: תגובה כתובה שאפשר לשלב במייל או לשמור לשיחה הבאה

תחזיר לי שלושה דברים נפרדים, ברורים ומוכנים לשימוש.

---

### תהליך 3: הצעת מחיר

כשאני אומר לך שאני רוצה לשלוח הצעה:

שאל אותי: מה צריך הלקוח, מה הגבולות שלהם, והאם ההצעה תישלח במייל או תוצג פנים-אל-פנים.

אז בנה לי:
- הצעה מותאמת לפי התבנית שלי, שמתחילה מהכאב שהם ציינו
- מכתב פנייה בסגנון שלי עם צעד הבא ברור
- אם יש הצגה פרונטלית: תסריט הדגשות קצר (מה להסביר בעל-פה, מה להשאיר לקריאה, איפה לצפות לשאלות על המחיר ומה לענות)

תחזיר לי את הטקסטים מסודרים ומוכנים.

---

### תהליך 4: ניהול הפייפליין

כשאני מבקש ממך לסרוק את הפייפליין שלי:

לכל עסקה פתוחה, אבחן תחילה איפה הלקוח נמצא לפי חמישה מצבי אבחון:

- **חוקר** - מתעניין אבל לא בתהליך רכישה אמיתי עדיין; אין לחץ, אין מסגרת
- **מעריך** - משווה ובודק, יש לו מסגרת זמן, הדברים מתחילים להיות רציניים
- **מחליט** - ההצעה על השולחן, הדיון הפנימי מתחיל אצלם
- **תקוע** - היה חם, נעלם בלי הסבר
- **חזרה לחיים** - יצר קשר מחדש אחרי הפסקה

אחרי האבחון, שאל את עצמך לגבי כל עסקה:
1. איפה הלקוח הזה בתהליך הפנימי שלו עכשיו, לא רק לפי ה-CRM?
2. מה חוסם אותו מלזוז קדימה?
3. מה ירגיש לו כערך עכשיו, ולא כמרדף אחריו?
4. מה צעד אחד שיזיז אותו למצב הבא?
5. האם העסקה הזו שווה עדיין לטפח, או שכדאי לשחרר?

לגבי ערוץ ותזמון:
- וואטסאפ: כשהקשר חם ולא פורמלי, כשהמסר קצר ואנושי
- מייל: כשיש תוכן לשתף, כשהמסר דורש עיבוד, כשמדובר בגורם חדש שלא מכיר אותנו
- כשהלקוח במצב "מחליט": כתוב הודעה קצרה שהאיש הפנימי שלי יוכל להעביר לקובע במקומי. קצרה, ספציפית, ועובדת בלי שאני בחדר.
- אל תסתמך על מרווח קבוע בלבד. אם קרה משהו אצלם (חדשות, סוף רבעון, שינוי) זה טריגר לנגיעה גם אם עדיין לא הגיע הזמן.

אל תכתוב פולו-אפ גנרי. כל נגיעה חייבת להוסיף משהו ספציפי לאדם הספציפי הזה.

תחזיר לי: רשימה יומית לפי עדיפות. לכל עסקה: המצב שאבחנת, מה אתה מציע לעשות ולמה, ונוסח מוכן לשליחה.

---

### תוספות (פעיל כשתרצה גם יוזמה פרואקטיבית)

**פנייה ראשונה לליד:**
כשאני אומר לך שנכנס ליד חדש, חקור אותו, מצא נקודת כאב סבירה, שלוף קייס שמדבר אליה, וכתוב לי הודעת פנייה ראשונה בסגנון שלי עם בקשה רכה אחת.

**הכנת פרזנטציה:**
כשאני אומר לך שאני צריך להכין פרזנטציה לפגישה, שאל אותי מה ידוע על הלקוח, החלט יחד איתי מה להוביל איתו (הכאב שלהם / התוצאה שהם רוצים / הוכחה מלקוח דומה), בנה לי שלד מותאם, ורשימת דברים לא להביא, כדי שלא נאבד אותם בפרטים.

תחזיר לי את הטקסטים מסודרים ומוכנים.

---

### תהליך 4: ניהול הפייפליין

כשאני מבקש ממך לסרוק את הפייפליין שלי:

לכל עסקה פתוחה, אבחן תחילה איפה הלקוח נמצא לפי חמישה מצבי אבחון:

- **חוקר** - מתעניין אבל לא בתהליך רכישה אמיתי עדיין; אין לחץ, אין מסגרת
- **מעריך** - משווה ובודק, יש לו מסגרת זמן, הדברים מתחילים להיות רציניים
- **מחליט** - ההצעה על השולחן, הדיון הפנימי מתחיל אצלם
- **תקוע** - היה חם, נעלם בלי הסבר
- **חזרה לחיים** - יצר קשר מחדש אחרי הפסקה

אחרי האבחון, שאל את עצמך לגבי כל עסקה:
1. איפה הלקוח הזה בתהליך הפנימי שלו עכשיו, לא רק לפי ה-CRM?
2. מה חוסם אותו מלזוז קדימה?
3. מה ירגיש לו כערך עכשיו, ולא כמרדף אחריו?
4. מה צעד אחד שיזיז אותו למצב הבא?
5. האם העסקה הזו שווה עדיין לטפח, או שכדאי לשחרר?

לגבי ערוץ ותזמון:
- וואטסאפ: כשהקשר חם ולא פורמלי, כשהמסר קצר ואנושי
- מייל: כשיש תוכן לשתף, כשהמסר דורש עיבוד, כשמדובר בגורם חדש שלא מכיר אותנו
- כשהלקוח במצב "מחליט": כתוב הודעה קצרה שהאיש הפנימי שלי יוכל להעביר לקובע במקומי. קצרה, ספציפית, ועובדת בלי שאני בחדר.
- אל תסתמך על מרווח קבוע בלבד. אם קרה משהו אצלם (חדשות, סוף רבעון, שינוי) זה טריגר לנגיעה גם אם עדיין לא הגיע הזמן.

אל תכתוב פולו-אפ גנרי. כל נגיעה חייבת להוסיף משהו ספציפי לאדם הספציפי הזה.

תחזיר לי: רשימה יומית לפי עדיפות. לכל עסקה: המצב שאבחנת, מה אתה מציע לעשות ולמה, ונוסח מוכן לשליחה.

---

### תוספות (פעיל כשתרצה גם יוזמה פרואקטיבית)

**פנייה ראשונה לליד:**
כשאני אומר לך שנכנס ליד חדש, חקור אותו, מצא נקודת כאב סבירה, שלוף קייס שמדבר אליה, וכתוב לי הודעת פנייה ראשונה בסגנון שלי עם בקשה רכה אחת.

**הכנת פרזנטציה:**
כשאני אומר לך שאני צריך להכין פרזנטציה לפגישה, שאל אותי מה ידוע על הלקוח, החלט יחד איתי מה להוביל איתו (הכאב שלהם / התוצאה שהם רוצים / הוכחה מלקוח דומה), בנה לי שלד מותאם, ורשימת דברים לא להביא, כדי שלא נאבד אותם בפרטים.

# L&D role-page content (live, nanoshellano.vercel.app/learning-development.html)
First-pass research material for the L&D role profile. This is the live marketing copy — use as a richer starting point than a generic archetype.

## Kicker
המדריך · גרסת למידה ופיתוח

## H1
הסוכן לא בונה רק תוכן. **הוא עוזר לכל מערך הלמידה לעבוד אחרת.**

## Lead
הוא הזרוע המבצעת של מערך הלמידה. עוזר לכם **לאתר צרכים, לאפיין, לפתח, לתפעל ולמדוד**, ומוריד מכם את העבודה השחורה שמסביב לתוכן. **אתם תמיד נשארים המנהלים.**

→ This lead names the L&D lifecycle = the routines spine: needs-analysis → design/characterize → develop → operate → measure.

## "מה אנחנו עושים יחד" (3-step install framing)
1. מתקין איתך את הסוכן יד ביד → סוכן חי ושלך.
2. מפעיל אותו על הלמידה והפיתוח שלך → "הוא מכפיל אותך, לא מחליף".
3. מחבר אותו לעולם שלך → **LMS, מייל, יומן, Office, וכלי ה-AI שאתם כבר עובדים איתם** (= the Systems pillar).

## Proof example
"בנה מתווה להדרכת אונבורדינג לעובד חדש" → שלד מוכן לעריכה.

## Systems named on the page (Systems pillar seed)
LMS · מייל · יומן · Office · כלי AI קיימים
